title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: GAIL'S KAYAK
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Gail Pritchard, fifty-seven, a county court clerk in Hot Springs, Arkansas.
For thirty years, she stamped papers and said, someday, I'll paddle Lake Ouachita.
Someday finally showed up. It cost forty dollars.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE YARD SALE
segments.quote: Life is what happens to us while we are making other plans.
segments.author: Allen Saunders
lines: One Saturday, Gail drove past a yard sale. A faded red kayak leaned on the fence.
She almost kept driving. She had plans. Laundry, mostly.
Then she remembered a line her dad clipped from Reader's Digest, by Allen Saunders:
Life is what happens to us while we are making other plans.
She paid forty dollars and tied the kayak to her little Corolla with a garden hose.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE CRANK
segments.quote: The man with a new idea is a Crank until the idea succeeds.
segments.author: Mark Twain
lines: On Monday, the whole clerk's office laughed.
Gail, you get seasick on a porch swing!
Her boss Darlene taped a note to her stamp pad, from Mark Twain:
The man with a new idea is a Crank until the idea succeeds.
Fine. She'd be a Crank. A Crank with a paddle.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE BOAT RAMP
segments.quote: And now that you don't have to be perfect, you can be good.
segments.author: John Steinbeck
lines: Her first morning, the kayak rolled, and Gail went under, in front of six bass fishermen.
Dolores, a retired park ranger, fished her out and quoted John Steinbeck:
And now that you don't have to be perfect, you can be good.
Everybody already saw the worst. So Gail stopped trying to look like a pro, and just paddled.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: SLOW WATER
segments.quote: The sea does not reward those who are too anxious, too greedy, or too impatient.
segments.author: Anne Morrow Lindbergh
lines: By week two, Gail wanted ten miles a day. She got blisters, and a sunburn shaped like Arkansas.
Dolores handed her an old book by the writer and pilot Anne Morrow Lindbergh:
The sea does not reward those who are too anxious, too greedy, or too impatient.
So she slowed down. One cove each morning. She met a heron, two otters, and one very rude goose.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE STORM
segments.quote: Courage is the resolution to face the unforeseen.
segments.author: Agatha Christie
lines: In August, Gail tried the big crossing. Halfway out, the wind kicked up and thunder rolled.
Her heart pounded. Then she thought of the Agatha Christie mystery in her dry bag:
Courage is the resolution to face the unforeseen.
She paddled to a little island and waited it out with a pimento cheese sandwich.
When the sky cleared, she finished the crossing.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE PADDLE CLUB
segments.quote: I think I have learned that the best way to lift one's self up is to help some one else.
segments.author: Booker T. Washington
lines: Back at work, Darlene asked, quietly, could you teach me?
Gail remembered words from Booker T. Washington, on a poster at the library:
I think I have learned that the best way to lift one's self up is to help some one else.
Now every Saturday, nine clerks paddle Lake Ouachita. They call themselves the Courthouse Cranks.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Stop planning. Be the Crank. Be good. Go slow. Face the storm. Bring a friend.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Stop waiting for someday. Let them laugh. Be good, not perfect. Go slow. Face the storm. And bring a friend.
Me, I tried a kayak once. The kayak won.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
